one_line_idea: Open-vocabulary detectors are effectively closed-vocabulary: novel-class success is concentrated on concepts frequent in web caption pretraining, and performance on genuinely caption-rare concepts collapses.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Per-class zero-shot detection quality is primarily predicted by concept frequency in the caption pretraining distribution rather than by benchmark-defined novelty, so claimed open-set generalization is mostly retrieval of pretrained name-appearance associations.

one_line_idea: Open-vocabulary detection AP is a property of the query vocabulary list, not the detector: adding or removing distractor class names materially changes scores and method rankings.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Reported AP values are unstable under reasonable changes to the query vocabulary, and the size of this instability exceeds typical gaps between competing methods, making vocabulary composition an uncontrolled experimental variable.

one_line_idea: Open-vocabulary detectors lack a calibrated none-of-the-above: their scores cannot express that a region matches no queried concept, causing systematic false positives when the true object is outside the vocabulary.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] When the true category of an object is absent from the query vocabulary, open-vocabulary detectors systematically relabel it as the nearest queried concept with high confidence, rather than suppressing it, and this failure is invisible in standard benchmarks whose vocabularies cover all annotated objects.

one_line_idea: Open-vocabulary detectors are context classifiers in disguise: pasting objects into atypical scenes collapses their naming accuracy far more than it collapses closed-vocabulary supervised detectors.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Open-vocabulary detectors rely more heavily on surrounding context for naming than supervised detectors do, so out-of-context objects are misnamed or missed at a disproportionately higher rate.

one_line_idea: Open vocabulary means English vocabulary: multilingual queries to open-vocabulary detectors degrade in proportion to the language's share of caption pretraining, even with multilingual text encoders.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Per-language detection quality for identical images and concepts tracks the language's representation in region-text alignment data, so non-English queries suffer systematic drops that the multilingual encoder does not repair, because alignment rather than text understanding is the bottleneck.

judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-C-103 (multilingual re-evaluation); kept for the frequency-proportionality law

one_line_idea: Per-class score incomparability breaks open-vocabulary deployment: a single global confidence threshold is near-meaningless because score distributions differ arbitrarily across queried names.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The optimal operating threshold varies so widely across queried classes that any single global threshold sacrifices a large fraction of achievable per-class F1, and simple per-class post-hoc calibration on a small labeled sample recovers most of it.

judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-C-011 (detection scores are not probabilities); kept as the OVD-specific operationalization

one_line_idea: A scene-prior skyline exposes benchmark weakness: an image-level classifier plus class-agnostic proposals matches open-vocabulary detectors on a large share of benchmark classes without any region-text alignment.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A deliberately crude skyline, image-level zero-shot classification for presence combined with class-agnostic proposals and simple heuristics for assignment, achieves a nontrivial fraction of open-vocabulary detection AP, and the classes where it matches full detectors are exactly where benchmarks fail to test region-level grounding.

one_line_idea: IoU is the wrong metric below a size threshold: center-distance-based matching reorders small-object detection methods and agrees better with human quality judgments.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For small objects, IoU-based matching measures pixel jitter rather than useful localization quality, so switching to a scale-appropriate criterion such as normalized center distance changes method rankings and matches human judgments of detection usefulness better.

one_line_idea: Sub-pixel translation reveals stride aliasing: small-object detection output oscillates strongly under tiny image shifts because object size interacts with feature stride, a deterministic and fixable artifact.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Detection confidence and even presence of small-object predictions oscillate quasi-periodically as the image is translated by sub-stride amounts, with amplitude growing as object size shrinks relative to stride, making a measurable fraction of small-object misses pure grid-alignment bad luck.

one_line_idea: Most claimed small-object method gains are pixel-budget effects: at equal effective input pixels on the object, specialized small-object techniques lose most of their advantage over plain high-resolution inference.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] When comparisons are controlled for effective pixels-on-object and total inference compute, a large fraction of reported small-object improvements shrinks toward zero, because the operative ingredient was resolution recovery rather than the proposed mechanism.

one_line_idea: Tiny-object classification is contextual inference, not appearance recognition: below a resolvable size, detectors name objects from scene context, and context-swap tests expose this hidden dependence.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For objects below an identifiable size threshold, detector class decisions are driven mostly by context rather than in-box evidence, so context manipulation flips tiny-object labels at a much higher rate than large-object labels, and benchmark tiny-object accuracy overstates appearance-based recognition.

one_line_idea: Dense-scene errors are dominated by duplicate and merge mistakes that AP barely registers: a dedicated identity-error metric reveals a failure axis invisible in current rankings.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Methods with similar AP on dense benchmarks differ widely in identity-error rates, merge, split, and duplicate mistakes, and these errors are what downstream tasks like tracking and counting actually suffer from, so an identity-error metric would reorder methods relative to AP for dense-scene use.

one_line_idea: Fixed query budgets create a silent recall cliff: query-based detectors fail abruptly when instance count approaches the query count, and the failure is invisible on benchmarks dominated by sparse images.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Recall of query-based detectors as a function of ground-truth instance count degrades sharply as the count approaches a fraction of the query budget, earlier than the nominal budget suggests, because queries compete and collapse onto duplicate hypotheses, and standard benchmark averages hide this cliff.

one_line_idea: Benchmark-defined small is not domain small: small-object method rankings established on natural-photo benchmarks invert on scale distributions typical of aerial or microscopy imagery.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Small-object techniques tuned on natural-photo size distributions exploit regime-specific properties, such as context availability and moderate density, so their relative ordering does not transfer to regimes where objects are a few pixels wide and context is homogeneous, and some celebrated techniques underperform simple baselines there.

judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-C-018 template (rankings invert across regimes); kept, distinct substrate

one_line_idea: Training assignment starves tiny objects: standard positive-sample assignment gives near-zero learning signal to the smallest objects, and oracle-assignment experiments would recover much of the small-object gap.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A disproportionate share of the small-object performance gap originates at training-time assignment rather than at representation or inference, so intervening only on assignment, giving tiny objects guaranteed positives, closes a large fraction of the gap without architectural change.

one_line_idea: Size priming in detection: small instances are found mainly when larger same-class instances co-occur in the image, and isolated small objects fail disproportionately, a bias hidden by co-occurrence-heavy benchmarks.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Detectors use large same-class instances as within-image evidence that primes detection of small ones, so small-instance recall conditioned on the presence of a larger same-class instance is substantially higher than recall for isolated small instances, and benchmark aggregates mask a much worse isolated-small performance.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Size priming: within-class co-occurrence gating small-object recall is not a template member; no other idea predicts detection conditioned on same-class scale context.

one_line_idea: Detectors hallucinate regularity in packed layouts: on grids of repeated identical objects, models fill in missing items at empty positions, revealing pattern-completion behavior in dense detection.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Detectors internalize layout periodicity and use it as evidence, so when an item is removed from an otherwise regular grid, models produce confident false positives at the vacated position at rates far above matched non-periodic controls, meaning dense-scene precision partly measures pattern completion rather than perception.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Pattern-completion hallucination in regular layouts: detectors filling in missing grid items is a generative-prior claim about discriminative models; unique failure family.

one_line_idea: Super-resolution preprocessing for small-object detection trades localization gains for classification bias: generative upsampling drags tiny-object labels toward visually typical categories.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Super-resolution preprocessing improves box localization for small objects but biases their classification toward categories whose textures the upsampler considers typical, so rare or atypical categories are systematically relabeled as common lookalikes after enhancement, a harm invisible in aggregate AP.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Generative super-resolution dragging tiny-object labels toward typical categories: a preprocessing-induced semantic bias claim nobody else makes.

one_line_idea: Long-tail detection gains from reweighting losses are mostly post-hoc calibration in disguise: per-class score recalibration of a plain baseline recovers the bulk of reported rare-class improvements.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Much of the rare-class AP improvement from specialized long-tail training reduces to correcting the score scale of rare classes, so applying cheap post-hoc per-class calibration to a vanilla detector reproduces most of the gain without any training change.

one_line_idea: Long-tail methods overfit the benchmark's frequency histogram: retesting under resampled tail shapes reveals that gains are tied to one particular class-frequency profile.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The gains of published long-tail methods are substantially specific to the tuned frequency profile, so re-creating the benchmark with a different tail shape by subsampling annotations reorders methods and shrinks average gains, revealing profile overfitting rather than general imbalance robustness.

one_line_idea: Copy-paste augmentation teaches paste detection: rare-class gains from copy-paste partly reflect boundary and compositing cues, and artifact-free insertion tests would show smaller true gains.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models trained with copy-paste partially learn to associate the target classes with compositing artifacts, so their measured rare-class improvement is inflated relative to their improvement on naturally photographed rare instances, and the inflation grows with how artifact-prone the augmentation pipeline is.

judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-B-087 (copy-paste compositing cues); kept for the long-tail gains-accounting design

one_line_idea: Repeat-factor sampling helps through contexts, not instances: oversampling images containing rare classes mostly benefits by re-exposing their scene contexts, which context-only controls can demonstrate.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A significant fraction of the benefit attributed to rare-instance repetition actually comes from re-exposure to rare-class contexts, so a control that oversamples similar contexts without the rare instances, or masks the instances during repeated epochs, retains much of the gain, revealing that the mechanism is context prior sharpening rather than instance learning.

one_line_idea: Average tail AP hides intra-tail regression: long-tail methods improve some rare classes while actively degrading others, and worst-group reporting would change which methods look best.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Existing long-tail methods redistribute performance within the tail, improving classes that suit their mechanism while hurting others below baseline, so worst-group and per-class-delta reporting would reveal method profiles that mean-based leaderboards conflate, and would reorder methods for applications caring about all rare classes.

one_line_idea: The tail gap decomposes into proposal recall versus classification differently than assumed: for unusual-shaped rare objects the real bottleneck is objectness transfer, not naming, inverting the standard decomposition.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The localization-transfers assumption holds only for tail classes that are geometrically typical, and for the subset of tail classes with atypical geometry, thin structures, extreme aspect ratios, or unusual scales, proposal recall is the dominant bottleneck, so the tail is heterogeneous and needs bifurcated treatment.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Anti-thesis to the shard's own naming-vs-finding consensus: objectness transfer, not naming, bottlenecks unusual-shaped rare objects. Protected as deliberate tension with D-071.

one_line_idea: Boxes already contain masks: frozen features of box-only detectors support high-quality mask prediction with tiny mask supervision, suggesting mask annotation budgets are largely wasted.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The information needed for accurate masks is already present in box-trained detector features, so a small mask head trained on a tiny fraction of mask labels atop frozen box-detector features approaches the mask quality of fully mask-supervised models, implying the marginal value of large-scale mask annotation is low.

one_line_idea: Segmentation-first detection wins on irregular objects: deriving boxes from class-agnostic masks beats box-first pipelines for thin, curved, and perforated objects, an advantage hidden by benchmark shape statistics.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For an identifiable shape subpopulation, boxes-from-masks pipelines outperform box-first ones on both localization and downstream usefulness, and mainstream benchmarks contain too few such objects for this advantage to register in overall AP, so pipeline-design conclusions drawn from benchmark averages are shape-biased.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Segmentation-first detection for irregular objects inverts the standard pipeline direction; benchmark shape statistics hiding it is a concrete confound claim.

one_line_idea: Interior-dominated mask metrics hide boundary failure: instance segmentation progress measured by mask IoU has plateaued at boundaries, and boundary-weighted evaluation reorders methods and better predicts downstream utility.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Ranking instance segmentation methods by boundary-focused metrics diverges materially from mask-IoU rankings, boundary quality has improved much more slowly than interior quality over recent method generations, and boundary metrics predict downstream task success better than mask IoU does.

one_line_idea: Detector-to-segmenter pipelines fail multiplicatively, not independently: promptable segmenters amplify detector box errors on exactly the hard instances, so pipeline quality is worse than the product of component qualities.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Detector box errors and prompt-conditioned segmentation errors are positively correlated on the same instances, occlusion, clutter, and ambiguous extent hurt both stages, so end-to-end mask quality is substantially below what independence-based composition of component metrics predicts, and component-wise model selection misranks full pipelines.

one_line_idea: Amodal-modal convention mismatch breaks detection-segmentation stacks under occlusion: components trained with different visibility conventions disagree precisely on occluded objects, and pipelines silently mix the two.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Detector boxes and segmenter masks in mixed-convention pipelines diverge systematically as occlusion increases, producing box-mask inconsistencies that harm downstream geometry estimates, and occlusion-stratified consistency measurement will expose which popular component combinations are convention-incompatible.

one_line_idea: Training detection through mask-derived objectives improves boxes themselves: replacing box regression targets with boxes derived from predicted masks yields better localization even measured by box AP on non-convex objects.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Predicting spatial support first and deriving boxes from it provides a better-posed learning signal, so mask-mediated box training improves box quality on irregular and occluded objects relative to direct box regression at matched supervision cost, because the intermediate representation aligns with actual evidence.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Mask-derived box targets improving box AP itself is a supervision-geometry claim running against the multitask framing; cheap and decisive.

one_line_idea: Instance segmentation systematically forbids nested instances: overlap-resolution heuristics assume quasi-disjoint objects, making object-inside-object cases a structural blind spot across current methods.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Current methods fail on nested-instance configurations at rates far above their overall error rates, the failure is caused by overlap-resolution machinery rather than by features, and benchmarks under-sample nesting so severely that this structural limitation has escaped measurement.

one_line_idea: Detection-segmentation multitask benefit is one-directional: detection supervision helps segmentation, but segmentation supervision adds little to detection at foundation scale, contradicting the mutual-benefit narrative.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] At current pretraining scale, the marginal benefit matrix between detection and segmentation supervision is strongly asymmetric, box supervision still improves mask tasks, while mask supervision contributes negligibly or negatively to box tasks, so joint-training design decisions based on old mutual-benefit results are miscalibrated.

one_line_idea: The thing-stuff boundary is a load-bearing arbitrary choice: reclassifying ambiguous categories between thing and stuff swings panoptic comparisons, so panoptic rankings partly measure ontology luck.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Method rankings under panoptic metrics are sensitive to the thing-stuff assignment of ambiguous categories, because architectures differ in relative instance versus semantic strength, so a plausible re-partition of the ontology changes leaderboard order, revealing that part of measured quality is fit to one ontology choice.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Thing-stuff ontology as load-bearing arbitrary choice attacks panoptic evaluation at the ontology level rather than the metric level.

one_line_idea: Dense pretraining transfers to detection through objectness, not classification: pixel-level pretraining gains concentrate in proposal recall, implying cheap class-agnostic dense objectives could replace expensive semantic ones.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The dominant channel of dense-pretraining benefit for detection is improved class-agnostic objectness and boundary sensitivity rather than improved region classification, so decomposed evaluation will locate the gains in proposal recall and localization precision, and a purely class-agnostic dense objective will match semantic dense pretraining for detection transfer.

one_line_idea: Attribute binding fails at the instance level in open-vocabulary detection: with two objects of swapped attributes in one scene, detectors match queries to the wrong instances at near-chance rates.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Region-text alignment does not repair compositional binding, so in scenes containing two instances whose attributes are exchanged, a red cup beside a blue plate versus a blue cup beside a red plate, queries specifying attribute-noun combinations select the correct instance barely above chance, even when each attribute and noun is individually well detected.

one_line_idea: Web-pretrained detectors hallucinate companion objects: scores for typically co-occurring categories are elevated even when absent, and this co-occurrence hallucination exceeds that of in-domain supervised detectors.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Foundation detectors assign systematically elevated detection scores to absent-but-typical companion objects, a keyboard near a monitor, a rider on a horse, relative to matched supervised detectors, and the effect strength is predictable from co-occurrence statistics of the pretraining distribution.

judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-C-089 (co-occurrence hallucination benchmarks); kept for the detector-level supervised-baseline comparison

one_line_idea: Foundation detector errors are correlated across model families: shared web data induces shared blind spots, so ensembling different foundation detectors yields far less error diversity than their architectural diversity suggests.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Instance-level error overlap between distinct foundation detector families substantially exceeds what accuracy-matched independence would predict, exceeds the overlap between supervised detectors trained on disjoint data, and concentrates on data-driven failure modes, so consensus among foundation models is much weaker evidence of correctness than assumed.

one_line_idea: Foundation detectors have a canonical-scale prior: objects photographed at atypical absolute scales, extreme close-ups or extreme distance, are missed in ways predicted by web photo composition statistics, and rescaling recovers them.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Foundation detectors encode a per-category canonical apparent-size prior, so detection performance as a function of object apparent size peaks near web-typical framing and degrades asymmetrically at atypical scales, and simple test-time rescaling toward the canonical size recovers a large share of the misses, proving the failure is a prior, not a feature limitation.

one_line_idea: Frozen foundation features hit a localization precision ceiling: high-IoU detection quality saturates regardless of head capacity, because image-level pretraining discards sub-patch spatial precision that fine-tuning must rebuild.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Detection heads on frozen foundation features show a characteristic signature, competitive low-IoU AP but a persistent deficit at high IoU thresholds that no head capacity increase closes, while modest backbone fine-tuning closes it quickly, demonstrating that precise extent information is absent from frozen features rather than merely unread.

one_line_idea: Foundation detectors have a web-aesthetic prior: semantically harmless but statistically atypical imaging conditions, unusual white balance, nonstandard aspect ratios, flash artifacts, degrade them more than matched supervised detectors.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Foundation detectors are tuned to web-typical image statistics beyond semantics, so distribution shifts that violate web aesthetics without harming semantic content cause disproportionate degradation relative to supervised detectors trained with aggressive photometric augmentation, and standard corruption benchmarks miss this axis entirely.

judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-A-059 family (web photo priors); kept for the imaging-statistics axis distinct from composition

one_line_idea: Multimodal LLMs are better detection verifiers than detectors: their box generation fails on coordinate production, not perception, so the generation-verification gap argues for verifier-role deployment.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For the same model and images, the accuracy of accepting or rejecting proposed boxes substantially exceeds the accuracy of generating boxes, the generation deficit traces to coordinate-production errors rather than perceptual failure, and a proposal-plus-LLM-verification pipeline therefore beats LLM-direct detection at matched compute.

one_line_idea: Multimodal LLM boxes betray tokenizer priors: generated coordinates cluster on round numbers and canonical aspect ratios, a measurable output-distribution distortion that standard AP evaluation never reveals.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Generated box distributions from multimodal LLMs exhibit strong spectral peaks at round coordinates, quantization-grid artifacts, and aspect-ratio modes absent from ground-truth distributions, these distortions bias which objects are localizable accurately, and distributional distortion severity predicts per-model localization quality on non-canonical geometry.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Tokenizer priors visible in generated box coordinates (round numbers, canonical aspect ratios) is an output-distribution artifact unique to autoregressive interfaces.

one_line_idea: Vocabulary forgetting outpaces domain gains: fine-tuning open-vocabulary detectors on narrow domains erases their broad-vocabulary competence at a rate that makes naive domain adaptation a net capability loss.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Open-vocabulary breadth degrades faster than domain performance improves along the fine-tuning trajectory, the forgetting is concentrated in the region-text alignment rather than the visual features, and the standard practice of picking checkpoints by domain validation silently selects near-maximal vocabulary damage.

one_line_idea: State breaks detectors before category does: foundation detectors fail on known objects in unusual states, overturned, disassembled, damaged, more than on unseen categories in canonical states.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The effective generalization frontier of foundation detectors is state-space, not category-space, so detection of common categories in atypical states is worse than detection of rare categories in typical states, inverting the field's implicit difficulty ordering and revealing state coverage as the binding constraint.

one_line_idea: At foundation scale, detection error is almost all recognition: class-agnostic localization is near ceiling, so architecture work on box mechanisms attacks a solved subproblem.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For modern large-backbone detectors, class-agnostic recall at moderate IoU with realistic proposal budgets is close to its ceiling on standard benchmarks, the overwhelming majority of residual AP loss traces to classification and scoring errors, and this recognition share has grown monotonically with backbone scale, implying localization-focused research now yields structurally diminishing returns.

one_line_idea: Localization and recognition want incompatible features: two-stream detectors reading separate frozen representations for where and what beat single-feature detectors at matched compute.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The shared-feature compromise measurably hurts both subtasks, so routing localization and recognition heads to separately optimized representations, one geometry-preserving, one semantics-preserving, outperforms shared-feature detectors at matched total compute, with the gain concentrated where the two demands conflict most, small objects and fine-grained classes.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Where/what feature incompatibility (two-stream frozen readout beating single features) contradicts both the shared-backbone default and this shard's recognition-only story. Protected tension.

one_line_idea: IoU-threshold sweeps fingerprint what a method actually improved: most claimed detection advances are either pure-recognition or pure-localization gains, and the sweep signature exposes mislabeled contributions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Classifying published methods by their AP-versus-IoU-threshold gain profiles yields a clean two-cluster structure, recognition-type and localization-type, the claimed mechanisms of a nontrivial fraction of methods mismatch their measured cluster, and the profile predicts transfer, recognition-type gains transfer across box conventions while localization-type gains do not.

one_line_idea: Detectors should output box uncertainty, not just label confidence: cheap per-coordinate uncertainty adds little AP but transforms downstream decision quality, exposing a metric-deployment mismatch.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Per-coordinate localization uncertainty estimated by lightweight heads is well correlated with realized box error, propagating it to downstream tasks improves their decisions substantially even though detection AP barely moves, and the field's AP monoculture is why such outputs remain nonstandard despite negligible cost.

one_line_idea: Detection classification is not crop classification: region labels depend on an optimal, class-specific amount of context, and both context-free crops and whole-image reasoning underperform the learned intermediate.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Classification accuracy on ground-truth boxes as a function of included context around the crop follows an inverted-U with a class-dependent optimum, strong image-level classifiers applied to tight crops lose substantially to detector-internal classification, and the optimal context ratio is predictable from class properties like size, context dependence, and confusability.

one_line_idea: Duplicate suppression is a recognition problem misassigned to geometry: identity-aware deduplication that asks are these the same object beats overlap-threshold suppression exactly where detection is hardest, adjacent identical objects.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The information that distinguishes two adjacent instances from duplicate hypotheses of one instance is appearance-level instance identity, invisible to geometry, so suppression informed by an instance-identity signal, learned from appearance correspondence, dominates geometric suppression on dense same-class scenes at equal budgets, while matching it elsewhere.

one_line_idea: A scene-statistics decision rule for counting: measurable image properties predict whether detection-based or regression-based counting will be more accurate on a given image, enabling per-image method routing.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Cheap per-image statistics, estimated density, size distribution, overlap structure, predict the sign of the accuracy difference between the two counting paradigms reliably enough that a learned router choosing per image beats either paradigm applied uniformly, by a margin that grows with workload heterogeneity.

one_line_idea: Multimodal LLM counting is subitizing plus guessing: exact counting holds up to a small integer and then collapses to density-conditioned estimation, a signature invisible in benchmarks that average over count ranges.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Model counting behavior decomposes into two regimes, near-exact performance up to a small threshold and coarse magnitude estimation beyond it, with errors in the second regime scaling with the true count and correlating with density cues rather than enumeration, so aggregate benchmark scores mask a qualitative capability boundary.

one_line_idea: Crowding suppresses per-instance recall independent of resolution: detection probability of an instance declines with the number of identical neighbors even when size and image quality are held constant.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Detectors exhibit a crowding effect analogous to the one documented in human peripheral vision, per-instance recall falls as identical-instance count rises even with size, spacing, and visibility controlled, driven by suppression machinery and by feature interference among similar neighbors rather than by pixel-level information limits.

one_line_idea: Counts are cheap detection supervision: adding per-image count labels for classes without box annotations improves detection of those classes, unlocking abundant inventory-style metadata as training signal.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Count labels constrain detector outputs strongly enough, through a differentiable counting consistency loss on predicted detections, to improve AP for count-supervised classes over both box-only baselines and image-level-tag weak supervision, because counts carry instance-multiplicity information that presence tags lack.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Count labels as cheap detection supervision unlocks a data source (inventory metadata) no other idea touches.

one_line_idea: Detector-regressor disagreement finds annotation errors: images where detection-based and density-based counts diverge are enriched for ground-truth mistakes, yielding a free annotation-audit signal.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Detection-based and density-based counters fail in nearly uncorrelated ways on model-difficult images but agree with each other when the annotation is wrong and the image is easy, so ranking images by paradigm disagreement with the annotation, conditioned on paradigm agreement with each other, concentrates annotation errors far above base rate, enabling targeted re-annotation.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Detector-regressor disagreement as a free annotation-error audit turns a nuisance (method disagreement) into an instrument.

one_line_idea: Class-averaged detection AP is driven by a volatile minority: bootstrap analysis shows overall benchmark rankings hinge on a handful of high-variance classes, making leaderboard stability an illusion.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The variance of headline AP is concentrated in a small set of low-instance-count classes, method rankings frequently reorder under test-set resampling because of exactly those classes, and reporting AP with class-stratified uncertainty or trimmed aggregation would change which methods appear to lead on established benchmarks.

one_line_idea: AP rewards unusable predictions: methods gain benchmark points from dense low-confidence box floods that no deployment threshold would keep, so operating-point metrics reorder detection leaderboards.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A measurable share of between-method AP differences on standard benchmarks comes from the low-confidence tail that deployment never uses, so ranking methods by fixed-false-positive-rate operating metrics changes their order, and some celebrated methods derive most of their advantage from tail-region behavior.

one_line_idea: Detection test sets are effectively smaller than they look: image-level and instance-level near-duplicates inflate effective sample size, understating uncertainty and overstating fine-grained method distinctions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Standard detection test sets contain enough near-duplicate imagery, repeated scenes, burst frames, recropped versions, that the effective independent sample size is substantially below the nominal count, so all uncertainty estimates are optimistic and some reported method distinctions fall inside the corrected noise floor.

judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-C-023/C-027 (duplicates and non-iid splits); kept for the variance (effective-n) consequence

one_line_idea: The default detection-count cap censors dense scenes: standard evaluation truncates predictions per image at a fixed limit, so performance on the densest images is systematically unmeasured and methods are blind-ranked there.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The prediction cap materially censors evaluation on high-instance-count images, methods differing specifically in dense-scene ability receive nearly identical scores because their differences are truncated away, and uncapped or density-scaled evaluation would reorder methods for dense-scene applications.

one_line_idea: Greedy confidence-ordered matching biases AP against certain prediction styles: optimal-assignment scoring changes per-method AP unevenly, revealing that part of measured differences is matching-algorithm artifact.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Methods whose confidence ranking correlates differently with localization quality are penalized differently by greedy matching, so re-scoring with optimal bipartite assignment shifts per-method AP unevenly, and some between-method gaps shrink or reverse, exposing a matching-rule component inside reported differences.

one_line_idea: Unreported inference-time enhancements account for a large share of detection leaderboard deltas: equal-inference-budget re-evaluation collapses many claimed architecture advantages.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Normalizing a representative slice of claimed method improvements to matched inference compute and identical test-time settings will eliminate or reverse a substantial fraction of the deltas, showing that a nontrivial part of perceived architectural progress is unstandardized inference-time expenditure.

one_line_idea: Benchmark precision is annotation-limited for top detectors: a substantial share of their scored false positives are correct detections of unannotated objects, so measured precision differences among strong models are annotation artifacts.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For current strong detectors on standard benchmarks, the fraction of scored false positives that are actually correct detections of unannotated objects is large enough that measured precision saturates against the annotation rather than against model ability, and between-model precision differences at the top of leaderboards mostly reflect differential alignment with annotation habits.

one_line_idea: Annotation conventions drift within datasets: box tightness and part-inclusion practices vary across annotation batches, and detectors learn the average, producing systematic per-batch evaluation bias.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Measurable annotation-style drift exists within standard detection datasets, recoverable by clustering annotation geometry statistics, models trained on the full data learn a style average that mismatches every batch, and evaluation error correlates with the batch-style distance from the average, meaning part of measured localization error is style mismatch rather than model imprecision.

judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-B-021/C-067 (convention decodability, instruction-dependent truth); kept for within-dataset batch drift

one_line_idea: Granularity-ambiguous aggregates drive outsized detection error: stacks, piles, and clusters annotated inconsistently as one-or-many account for a disproportionate share of both false positives and misses.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Instances belonging to ambiguous aggregates carry error rates several times the dataset average for strong detectors, the errors are dominated by decomposition mismatch rather than detection failure, and excluding or tolerance-scoring the aggregate stratum meaningfully changes both absolute scores and method rankings.

one_line_idea: High-IoU evaluation operates beyond the human agreement floor: inter-annotator box IoU distributions show that strict-threshold metrics score models against noise, and noise-floor-normalized metrics change conclusions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The distribution of inter-annotator IoU varies strongly by object size, boundary clarity, and occlusion, strict-threshold metrics frequently demand agreement beyond the human floor for whole object strata, and normalizing thresholds by the measured local noise floor produces materially different model scores and method orderings in the precision regime.

one_line_idea: Detectors out-localize their own training labels: model predictions are systematically closer to multi-annotator consensus than the single-annotator boxes they were trained and evaluated on, so evaluation penalizes models for being right.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For well-trained detectors, predicted boxes lie closer to multi-annotator consensus geometry than the original single-annotator ground truth does, so a measurable fraction of scored localization error is actually the label's error, and evaluating against consensus would raise measured model quality and differentially re-rank methods by their denoising ability.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Models out-localizing their own training labels (closer to consensus than single-annotator GT) implies evaluation penalizes correctness; sharpest annotation-noise claim in the shard.
judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-C-066 (agreement-ceiling reframing); kept for the consensus-outperformance design

one_line_idea: Model confusion matrices partially replicate annotator confusion: class-label errors in detection datasets are structured by visual similarity and annotation workflow, and models inherit these exact confusions, inflating measured semantic error.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The label-error confusion structure of a dataset, estimable from re-annotation samples, aligns measurably with the confusion structure of models trained on it, beyond what visual similarity alone predicts, so part of measured classification error reflects faithful learning of annotation mistakes, and cleaning training labels would reduce exactly the aligned confusions.

one_line_idea: Sparse-annotation training teaches contextual self-censorship: detectors trained under incomplete labeling learn context-dependent suppression of valid detections, producing deployment blind spots that complete-annotation fine-tuning reverses.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The false-negative supervision of sparse annotation is context-structured, certain categories are systematically under-labeled in certain scene types, so detectors learn scene-conditional suppression rules, detecting an object in one context and suppressing the same appearance in another, and these learned blind spots persist invisibly because evaluation shares the annotation sparsity.

one_line_idea: Open-vocabulary segmentation leaderboards measure mask-proposal quality, not language grounding: swapping the text encoder barely moves scores while swapping the class-agnostic mask generator moves them dramatically.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Variance in benchmark scores across published systems is dominated by the proposal stage, so cross-system comparisons mostly rank mask generators rather than grounding methods.

one_line_idea: Two-stage segment-then-classify pipelines are structurally biased against stuff categories because cropping a region for classification destroys exactly the context that defines stuff.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The crop-and-classify interface causes a systematic thing-versus-stuff performance asymmetry that is a property of the interface, not of the underlying VLM's knowledge.

one_line_idea: Training-free attention-surgery methods for dense CLIP-style inference gain mostly by spatially denoising features, and simple spatial smoothing of unmodified features recovers much of their improvement.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A substantial fraction of these gains comes from generic spatial regularization of noisy patch maps rather than from genuinely improved patch-to-text alignment.

one_line_idea: Text-to-patch similarity maps in contrastive VLMs localize by visual salience rather than by language: irrelevant text queries still highlight the same salient object.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A large component of these heatmaps is query-independent salience, so grounding demonstrations conflate language conditioning with generic foreground detection.

one_line_idea: Class-agnostic mask generators impose a granularity prior that mismatches linguistic category boundaries, capping open-vocabulary segmentation regardless of grounding quality.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A measurable fraction of open-vocabulary segmentation error is granularity mismatch, cases where no available proposal aligns with the linguistically correct region, and this fraction is invariant to improvements in region classification.

one_line_idea: Dense language-grounding quality scales with caption richness (words and noun phrases per image) rather than raw pair count, making data curation for dense tasks orthogonal to curation for classification.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Holding pair count fixed, pretraining on densely descriptive captions yields markedly better patch-level language alignment than sparsely captioned data, because multi-noun captions force sub-image correspondences.

one_line_idea: Retrieval-based dense labeling, transferring labels from retrieved segmented neighbors in frozen VLM feature space, can rival learned open-vocabulary segmentation heads while being training-free and instantly extensible.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Nearest-neighbor transfer of masks from a labeled support corpus via patch-level correspondence in frozen VLM space recovers most of the accuracy of trained open-vocabulary heads, indicating the heads mostly re-implement retrieval.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Training-free retrieval-based dense labeling as a rival to learned heads is a non-parametric contrarian baseline, not an audit template.

one_line_idea: Language-grounded segmenters lean on scene-context correlations so strongly that they segment object regions correctly even when the object itself is erased, revealing context-driven rather than evidence-driven masks.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Open-vocabulary segmenters produce substantially unchanged masks for a queried object after the object's pixels are inpainted away, in proportion to the class's contextual predictability.

one_line_idea: Prompt ensembling, a free win for zero-shot classification, is a mixed blessing for dense prediction: it helps region interiors but systematically blurs boundaries by averaging spatially incompatible similarity maps.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Different templates induce systematically different spatial supports for the same class, so embedding averaging trades boundary precision for interior recall in dense tasks.

one_line_idea: Fine-tuning VLMs on segmentation data narrows the open vocabulary at pixel level much faster than at image level, so standard image-level forgetting checks certify models that have already lost dense open-vocabulary ability.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Vocabulary forgetting is granularity-dependent: pixel-level alignment for unseen classes collapses earlier in fine-tuning than image-level alignment, because dense losses overwrite patch geometry while sparing the pooled embedding.

one_line_idea: Referring expression segmentation benchmarks are largely solvable by detecting the head noun and picking the most salient instance, so reported scores overstate relational language understanding.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A deliberately language-lobotomized baseline that extracts only the head noun and selects the largest or most salient matching instance captures a large fraction of benchmark performance, bounding how much relational understanding scores can actually reflect.

one_line_idea: Referring segmentation models collapse to near-chance instance selection precisely when relational clauses are necessary, and benchmarks should be stratified by distractor count to expose this.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Model accuracy conditioned on the number of same-category distractors decays steeply, with instance selection among many identical-category candidates approaching chance once appearance cues are uninformative.

one_line_idea: Referring models fail to ground text-dependent references (objects identified by written labels in the image) even when the same system reads that text correctly in a question-answering mode, revealing an OCR-grounding integration gap.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Reading text and grounding masks are served by weakly integrated pathways, so expressions whose disambiguation requires reading in-image text produce near-chance instance selection despite intact reading ability verified separately.

one_line_idea: No-target referring, correctly refusing to segment when the expression matches nothing, is the dominant unsolved failure mode: models confidently produce masks for absent referents.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Existing referring models, including those with explicit no-target training, have refusal operating points that collapse under mild domain shift, because absence detection relies on dataset-specific score calibration rather than genuine evidence assessment.

one_line_idea: Multi-target and exception referring expressions break single-instance architectural priors: models emit exactly one mask because their decoders structurally assume one referent.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Set-referring failure is architectural rather than linguistic: models represent the correct set internally (recoverable by probing) but the single-mask decoding interface forces an arbitrary instance choice.

one_line_idea: Round-trip referring, where a model generates an expression for a region and then must comprehend its own expression, exposes grounding gaps invisible to standard one-way evaluation.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Round-trip failure, where a model cannot locate the region its own generated expression describes, is common and concentrates on relational and fine-grained expressions, indicating generation and comprehension use inconsistent internal groundings.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Round-trip self-consistency (comprehend your own generated expression) is a self-communication probe no benchmark currently runs.

one_line_idea: Referring segmentation built on multimodal LLMs is bottlenecked by vision-encoder resolution, not language reasoning: failures concentrate on small referents regardless of expression clarity.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Conditioning referring accuracy on referent pixel area will reveal a resolution wall below which performance collapses independently of linguistic complexity, and the wall tracks the encoder's effective patch footprint across model variants.

one_line_idea: Referring models fail on novel attribute-object combinations at segmentation time even when both the attribute and the object are individually well-grounded, exposing missing compositional binding in dense grounding.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dense grounding accuracy on unseen attribute-object pairs drops sharply relative to seen pairs with matched visual difficulty, because grounding relies on memorized pair co-occurrence rather than compositional binding.

one_line_idea: Per-pixel abstention, the option to label a pixel as none-of-the-provided-classes, is where all open-vocabulary segmenters fail, and it is unmeasured because benchmarks force total assignment.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models given an explicit abstention option either abstain almost never or almost everywhere depending on thresholding, because contrastive similarity scores lack an absolute scale that separates covered from uncovered pixels.

one_line_idea: Contrastive pretraining's learned temperature makes pixel-level similarity scores relative rankings rather than probabilities, so open-set pixel calibration requires anchoring scores to an absolute alignment reference.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Pixel-label confidence derived from softmaxed cosine similarities is systematically uncalibrated in ways predictable from the contrastive objective, and calibration transfers poorly across images because the score scale is image-dependent.

one_line_idea: Vocabulary-granularity mismatch is a dominant unmeasured error source: models are marked wrong for answering at a different but correct level of the concept hierarchy, and hierarchy-aware scoring reranks methods.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A substantial fraction of measured open-vocabulary segmentation error consists of hierarchy-consistent answers, and correcting the metric with hierarchy-aware credit changes method rankings because methods differ in granularity bias.

one_line_idea: Synonym inconsistency is a cheap unforgiving audit: querying the same class by different correct names yields materially different masks, and consistency across synonyms could be enforced as a free constraint.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Mask variation across synonyms of the same class is large, systematic, and predictable from caption-frequency differences between the synonyms, and enforcing synonym consistency at inference improves accuracy without any training.

judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-C-052 (synonym instability); kept for the pixel-level consistency-enforcement constraint

one_line_idea: Rare-class pixel labeling is governed by name statistics rather than visual difficulty: classes with common visual appearance but rare names underperform classes with rare appearance but common names.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Lexical rarity dominates visual rarity as a predictor of open-vocabulary dense accuracy, in contrast to supervised segmentation where visual factors dominate, revealing that the text tower is the binding constraint.

one_line_idea: Unseen-category generalization claims in open-vocabulary segmentation are inflated because unseen classes are visually near seen ones; stratifying by visual distance to the seen set reveals sharply weaker true generalization.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Reported unseen-class performance is concentrated on unseen classes with near neighbors in the seen set, and performance decays steeply with feature-space distance from the seen classes, exposing interpolation rather than generalization.

judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-C-024 (seen-shot); kept for class-level visual-distance stratification vs image-level exposure

one_line_idea: Anomaly segmentation via abstract text queries fails because contrastive text encoders cannot ground non-referential language: queries like unusual or out-of-place behave as near-noise directions in alignment space.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Similarity maps for abstract anomaly vocabulary carry little information about actual anomalies, performing near permutation-control levels, because the text embeddings of such terms have no stable visual grounding.

one_line_idea: Open-vocabulary segmentation degradation in specialist domains is driven more by the text tower than the vision tower: domain terms are poorly embedded, and text-side interventions recover more than image-side ones.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For a meaningful share of specialist-domain failure, the vision features already separate the relevant structures, but domain terminology embeds far from those features, so text-side fixes (definitional paraphrases, glossary-augmented prompts) outperform image-side adaptation at equal cost.

one_line_idea: VLM patch features lack mid-range context integration: they are simultaneously too global for instance boundaries and too local for stuff coherence, and the missing scale is measurable and fixable at inference.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Both symptoms share one cause: the effective receptive field distribution of VLM patch features has a deficit at intermediate scales, and inference-time multi-scale feature mixing targeted at that deficit fixes both symptoms simultaneously.

one_line_idea: Resolution-scaling tricks for dense inference silently corrupt text alignment: interpolating position embeddings improves geometry while drifting patch features away from the text tower's expected distribution.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Position-embedding interpolation shifts the patch-feature distribution off the manifold the text alignment was calibrated to, producing class-dependent alignment drift that partially cancels the geometric gains, especially for classes whose scores were marginal.

one_line_idea: Sliding-window dense inference produces label inconsistencies for the same object across windows, and lightweight global conditioning eliminates a class of errors that post-hoc blending merely hides.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Window-local ambiguity resolves differently across windows for the same object, creating contradictions that blending averages into low-confidence mush rather than resolving, and injecting cheap global context tokens into each window resolves them at the source.

one_line_idea: Anisotropy of contrastive patch embeddings makes cosine similarity a low-information ranking signal densely, and simple whitening of patch features reorders and improves pixel-label decisions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Patch-embedding anisotropy is more severe than image-embedding anisotropy and injects a query-independent bias into dense scores, so post-hoc whitening or spectral normalization of patch features yields systematic dense gains without touching the text tower.

one_line_idea: Multimodal LLMs contain more spatial detail than their language outputs use: pixel-probing their vision features beats their own verbalized dense answers, locating dense failure at the interface rather than in perception.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Linear or shallow probes on the frozen visual token stream inside a multimodal LLM recover substantially more dense information (boundaries, part locations, instance separation) than the model's own generated answers express, demonstrating an interface bottleneck between visual tokens and language decoding.

one_line_idea: Segmentation-capable multimodal LLMs hallucinate masks for absent objects at rates far exceeding their question-answering hallucination rates, making dense hallucination the field's most undermeasured risk.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The mask-decoding pathway bypasses whatever calibration curbs verbal hallucination, so asking a model to segment an absent object yields a confident mask more often than asking whether the object is present yields a false yes.

one_line_idea: Language-grounded segmenters are internally inconsistent about amodal versus modal extent: whether occluded object parts are included depends on the query phrasing and the occluder's category, not on any coherent convention.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models trained on visible-pixel masks but language-aligned to whole-object concepts produce inconsistent occlusion handling that varies with prompt wording, occluder type, and occlusion fraction, revealing an unresolved conflict between mask supervision and linguistic semantics.

one_line_idea: Aspect-ratio deviation from pretraining crops damages dense predictions much more than global ones: padding, squeezing, and tiling choices at inference are a silent variance source dense benchmarks never control.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dense metrics degrade nonlinearly with aspect-ratio distortion and the degradation exceeds the corresponding image-level effect, so unreported preprocessing choices contribute materially to cross-paper dense score differences.

one_line_idea: The best-aligned layer for dense prediction differs systematically by query type (things versus stuff, objects versus parts), so any single-layer feature choice is guaranteed suboptimal and query-adaptive layer selection is free accuracy.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Optimal extraction depth is a stable function of query semantics, with stuff and material queries peaking earlier and object and part queries peaking later, enabling a lightweight query-conditioned layer router that beats every fixed layer.

one_line_idea: The confusion matrix of an open-vocabulary segmenter is largely predictable from text-encoder geometry alone, before any image is processed, making text-side audits a cheap proxy for dense error analysis.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Pairwise class confusion mass in dense predictions is strongly predicted by text-embedding similarity between class names, with visual similarity adding surprisingly little once text geometry is accounted for.

one_line_idea: Hub class names, text embeddings abnormally close to many patch features, absorb pixels from many true classes, and hubness-correction techniques from retrieval transfer directly to dense labeling as training-free gains.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A small set of class names act as hubs in each vocabulary, capturing pixel mass far beyond their true prevalence, and applying retrieval-style hubness corrections to the pixel-to-text assignment reduces this systematic error across models.

one_line_idea: Class-name token length biases dense similarity magnitudes, so multi-word categories are systematically under- or over-predicted, and length normalization is a missing preprocessing step in every open-vocabulary pipeline.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Embedding norm and effective similarity scale correlate with name token length, injecting a length-dependent prior into pixel assignment that is unrelated to visual evidence and correctable by per-class score standardization.

one_line_idea: Polysemous class names produce sense-blended text embeddings that corrupt dense predictions, and sense-disambiguating prompt contexts recover accuracy on quietly polysemous benchmark classes.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For polysemous class names, the blended embedding sits between visual senses, depressing dense accuracy relative to a sense-pinned prompt, and the accuracy loss is predictable from sense-distribution statistics in web text.

one_line_idea: Contrastive text encoders barely encode spatial-relational words: removing them from referring expressions leaves the text embedding nearly unchanged, mechanistically explaining relation-blind dense grounding.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The embedding displacement caused by deleting or swapping spatial-relational words is small relative to displacement from content-word changes, and this text-side insensitivity quantitatively predicts each model's relational grounding failure rate.

one_line_idea: Negation invariance of contrastive text embeddings transfers directly into dense prediction: negated queries produce near-identical similarity maps to affirmative ones, and the embedding distance between a phrase and its negation predicts which models can be fixed by prompting alone.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The cosine distance between affirmative and negated forms of the same query is a strong predictor of a system's dense negation accuracy, separating systems fixable by prompt rewording from systems requiring text-tower surgery.

one_line_idea: Attribute-binding failure is text-side measurable: swapped-attribute expressions embed nearly identically in contrastive towers, and this bag-of-words geometry upper-bounds dense binding accuracy no matter how good the vision tower is.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The embedding distance between attribute-swapped expression pairs upper-bounds dense binding performance: systems whose text towers collapse swapped pairs cannot exceed chance on binding-critical dense queries, and the bound is tight empirically.

one_line_idea: Cross-lingual dense inconsistency, where translated class names yield different masks on the same image, is large, systematic, and a free multilingual audit for text-tower quality in dense pipelines.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Mask agreement across translated queries varies widely by language and class, tracks language share in pretraining text, and cross-lingual disagreement on unlabeled images predicts per-language dense accuracy without any labels.

judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-C-103; kept for the label-free cross-lingual consistency instrument

one_line_idea: Dense grounding models resolve frame-of-reference ambiguity by always choosing the viewer-centric reading, and benchmarks silently reward this because annotators did too, hiding a genuine ambiguity the field has never measured.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models exhibit a rigid viewer-centric policy regardless of contextual cues that humans use to switch frames, and measured spatial-grounding accuracy overstates competence because benchmark annotations share the same default.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Frame-of-reference ambiguity resolved silently viewer-centric, with annotators sharing the bias, claims a hidden agreement artifact between models and ground truth.

one_line_idea: Dense grounding handles canonical categorical relations but fails graded and metric spatial language: nearest, halfway, and almost-touching ground at near-chance despite high scores on left-right-above benchmarks.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models implement categorical relations as learned 2D templates and possess no graded spatial computation, so performance collapses precisely when the relation requires comparing continuous distances rather than matching a template.

one_line_idea: Relational grounding accuracy decays superlinearly with scene clutter because models approximate relations with global position priors that collapse when many candidates occupy every image region.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models ground relations via absolute image-position priors (left-of resolving to left-half-of-image) rather than relative geometry between the mentioned objects, a strategy whose accuracy collapses combinatorially as clutter grows.

one_line_idea: Depth-dependent relations fail because VLM features encode little metric depth, and supplying monocular depth as an auxiliary input disproportionately repairs behind and in-front-of while leaving 2D relations unchanged, cleanly attributing the failure.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The error profile of dense grounding is dimensionally structured: 2D relations succeed and depth relations fail in proportion to the features' measurable depth content, and depth-input injection acts as a targeted intervention validating the causal account.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Monocular-depth injection disproportionately repairing depth-dependent relations is a clean causal-attribution design, not a permutation.

one_line_idea: Relative-size references ground by image-plane area rather than real-world size: models pick the object with more pixels, failing whenever perspective makes the physically larger object smaller in the frame.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dense grounding models implement size comparatives as pixel-area comparisons with no depth correction, so their accuracy on size expressions inverts on perspective-conflict cases where the physically larger object is farther away.

one_line_idea: Dense grounding models trained on web photos fail systematically on egocentric viewpoints, and the failure is viewpoint-distributional rather than object-level: the same objects ground fine in third-person views.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Grounding degradation on egocentric imagery persists after controlling for object category and image quality, indicating a viewpoint-distribution gap in dense alignment rather than a recognition gap, and small amounts of egocentric-aligned data close it disproportionately fast.

one_line_idea: Grounding accuracy decays multiplicatively per relational hop in nested expressions, and measuring the per-hop decay factor gives a single scalar that predicts model behavior on arbitrarily complex referring chains.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Each additional relational hop multiplies success probability by a roughly constant model-specific factor, so complex-expression performance is predictable from single-hop measurements, and apparent architecture differences on hard benchmarks reduce to differences in this one factor.

one_line_idea: Spatial terms function as tie-breakers, not constraints: models first shortlist referents by appearance and only consult spatial language when appearance ties, an order of operations exposable by appearance-spatial conflict stimuli.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dense grounding operates lexicographically, appearance first and space second, so when spatial language contradicts the best appearance match, models follow appearance at high rates rather than integrating both cues probabilistically as listeners do.

one_line_idea: Background-region conventions are inconsistent across dense benchmarks and methods, and harmonizing background handling alone shifts reported open-vocabulary gaps enough to change some published conclusions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Interaction between per-benchmark background conventions and per-method background capabilities injects systematic score distortions, favoring methods whose failure modes align with each benchmark's convention, and a harmonized protocol changes cross-paper comparisons materially.

one_line_idea: A query-in-the-wild protocol, evaluating dense models on free-form user queries collected without benchmark vocabulary constraints, would reveal a large gap between benchmark scores and experienced quality.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Model success rates on genuinely free-form queries are far below benchmark scores on the same images, and failures cluster in query types (functional descriptions, pragmatic ellipsis, uncommon granularities) that benchmark vocabularies structurally exclude.

one_line_idea: Self-training with VLM-generated pseudo-masks amplifies text-side biases round over round: classes favored by text geometry gain pixels each iteration, and the drift is measurable, predictable, and correctable with text-side debiasing.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Iterative self-training compounds text-geometry biases multiplicatively, expanding hub-class pixel share and shrinking crowded-neighborhood classes each round, with drift rate predictable from initial text-side statistics.

judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-A-102 (bias amplification); kept for the text-side drift mechanism and text-debiasing intervention

one_line_idea: The missing dense alignment in contrastive VLMs is a shallow, learnable transform: a small frozen-backbone decoder trained on limited data recovers most of the gap to full fine-tuning, showing the information was present but misformatted.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The dense-task gap between frozen and fine-tuned backbones is mostly attributable to a fixable feature-formatting mismatch (spatial mixing, scale composition, alignment recalibration) learnable by a compact decoder, not to missing information in frozen features.

one_line_idea: Patch-level contrastive alignment objectives are ill-posed at boundaries because patches straddle classes, and boundary-aware assignment during training removes a systematic soft-boundary artifact that plagues all patch-supervised dense models.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Single-target patch supervision at boundaries causes characteristic boundary softening and class bleeding in trained models, and mixture-target or subpatch-weighted objectives eliminate the artifact with measurable boundary-metric gains at no interior cost.

one_line_idea: Fine-tuning the text tower for dense tasks is more damaging to open-vocabulary ability than fine-tuning the vision tower: alignment forgetting is asymmetric across towers, and freezing choice should follow the asymmetry.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Text-tower updates on narrow-vocabulary dense data distort the global text manifold, damaging alignment for all unsupervised names, while vision-tower updates generalize benignly across the visual domain, producing a strong retention asymmetry favoring frozen text towers.

one_line_idea: Training dense models on synthetic captions transfers the captioner's blind spots as a hard ceiling: student dense performance per concept is bounded by the teacher captioner's mention behavior, creating invisible inherited gaps.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Concepts the teacher captioner rarely mentions receive proportionally weak dense alignment in the student regardless of visual prevalence, so teacher mention statistics predict student per-concept dense accuracy, and diversifying teachers measurably lifts the inherited floor.

one_line_idea: Mixing instance-mask and semantic-mask supervision teaches conflicting notions of object extent, and the conflict measurably hurts referring tasks that need instances, suggesting supervision-type should be conditioned, not pooled.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Pooled training on conflicting extent conventions produces models with unstable instance-versus-region behavior, harming instance-critical tasks like referring segmentation, and conditioning the model on the intended convention via a task token recovers the loss.

one_line_idea: Part queries retrieve wholes: language-grounded segmenters asked for object parts return whole-object masks because caption supervision represents parts as attributes of wholes rather than as spatial units.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Part-query failure follows a specific signature, near-correct object selection with near-total part-boundary failure, indicating that part names are aligned to whole-object regions in feature space, and part-specific evaluation will show this signature across model families.

one_line_idea: Natural-language granularity cues (the whole X, just the Y of the X) fail to control mask extent reliably, while an explicit granularity token interface succeeds, showing granularity is representable but not language-accessible.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dense models represent multiple granularities internally, but linguistic granularity cues fail to select among them reliably, so structured granularity conditioning outperforms even carefully engineered phrasings by a wide margin.

one_line_idea: Predicted part and whole masks violate containment at high rates, and enforcing part-whole consistency at inference is a free accuracy and trustworthiness gain no current system exploits.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Containment violations between independently predicted part and whole masks are frequent, correlate strongly with error in at least one of the two masks, and projecting predictions onto the containment-consistent set improves both masks on average.

one_line_idea: Open-vocabulary segmenters exhibit basic-level bias: superordinate queries like animal produce worse masks than basic-level names for the same regions, because caption language overwhelmingly uses basic-level terms.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dense alignment strength varies systematically across abstraction levels with a peak at the basic level, so superordinate and subordinate queries for identical regions yield measurably worse masks, in proportion to each level's caption usage frequency.

one_line_idea: Stuff-stuff boundary placement is learned as dataset convention, not visual inference: models transfer their training dataset's boundary style to new domains, and cross-dataset boundary disagreement quantifies this hidden convention learning.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models reproduce their dense-training dataset's stuff-boundary conventions on foreign domains, so cross-dataset stuff-boundary error contains a systematic convention component separable from perceptual error, and convention adaptation with tiny calibration data recovers it.

one_line_idea: Linguistic countability drives segmentation topology: mass-noun phrasing yields merged regions and count-noun phrasing yields instance-like masks for the same visual material, an unmeasured coupling between grammar and mask structure.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Mask connectivity and instance structure vary systematically with the query's countability syntax rather than only with visual evidence, revealing that output topology is partly a linguistic artifact, exploitable for control but dangerous when unnoticed.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Grammar-to-topology coupling (mass vs count phrasing switching merged vs instance masks) is an unmeasured linguistic-structural effect; kept despite wave1 B-030 adjacency because topology switching differs from grounding-quality differences.
judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-B-030 (mass vs count nouns); kept for the topology-switching prediction

one_line_idea: Ordinal reference (the second cup from the left) grounds at near-chance across dense models because ordinal computation requires an explicit sort the architectures never perform, and errors follow a predictable off-by-adjacency pattern.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dense grounding lacks any mechanism to enumerate and rank candidate instances along an axis, so ordinal accuracy will sit near the chance level given the candidate count, with errors concentrated on adjacent ranks rather than random, indicating partial but insufficient ordering signal.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Ordinal reference failing for want of an explicit sort, with off-by-adjacency error structure, is an architectural-computation-gap claim with a distinctive predicted error signature.

one_line_idea: Instance counts derived from language-grounded segmentation systematically undercount in crowded scenes with a density-dependent bias, and the bias curve is stable enough to invert for calibrated counting.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Undercounting bias grows smoothly with true instance density and inter-instance overlap, is stable across scene types for a fixed model, and can be estimated once and inverted to produce calibrated counts with quantified uncertainty.

one_line_idea: Complement queries (everything except the sky) fail despite being trivially computable from the affirmative mask, exposing that dense systems lack a negation-as-set-operation pathway even where no perception is required.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dense systems fail complement queries at high rates while succeeding on the corresponding affirmative queries, demonstrating that failure is located purely in linguistic-operational parsing, and a lightweight query-rewriting layer that detects set operations and composes affirmative masks fixes it completely.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Complement queries failing despite being trivially computable from the affirmative mask isolates a set-operation gap with zero perceptual excuse.

one_line_idea: Attribute-only queries (everything red) are object-mediated: models find red objects but miss red stuff and red object-parts, revealing that attributes are grounded through object nouns rather than as pixel properties.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dense responses to bare-attribute queries will cover attribute-bearing objects while systematically missing attribute-bearing stuff regions and parts, with the miss rate predicting a general principle that dense grounding routes through object-noun representations.

one_line_idea: Comparative attribute grounding (the darker of the two) is near chance because per-pixel scoring has no cross-instance normalization step, and adding an explicit candidate-comparison stage fixes it without touching the backbone.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Independent-scoring architectures cannot represent relative comparisons, so comparative-query accuracy will hover near random selection among candidates, and a lightweight external stage that extracts per-candidate property values and compares them will restore high accuracy using the same backbone.

one_line_idea: Dense systems treat conjunctive and disjunctive queries identically: cats and dogs versus cats or dogs produce indistinguishable masks, revealing that logical connectives are dropped at the grounding interface.
