core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Predicted masks for conjunction and disjunction over the same class pair will be statistically indistinguishable across current systems, because text encoders compress both to similar embeddings and mask decoders have no set-semantics pathway.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Conjunction/disjunction indistinguishability (cats and dogs vs cats or dogs) is a logical-connective claim distinct from negation.

one_line_idea: Autoregressive coordinate emission for dense outputs accumulates spatial error along the sequence: later polygon vertices and later boxes in a list are systematically less accurate, an interface artifact invisible to aggregate metrics.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Spatial accuracy decays with sequence position within a single structured output, because early errors condition later predictions and attention to visual evidence dilutes as text context grows, producing a measurable within-output error gradient.

one_line_idea: Chain-of-thought reasoning before mask emission can hurt grounding: reasoning tokens displace visual attention, and mask accuracy on perceptually easy targets drops when models are made to think longer.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For perceptually direct targets, long reasoning traces interpose text context that dilutes attention to visual tokens at mask-decoding time, creating a reasoning tax measurable as accuracy loss that grows with trace length on easy cases while possibly helping hard relational cases.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Chain-of-thought actively harming mask grounding via attention displacement runs against the more-reasoning-is-better default.
judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-C-060 (CoT null); kept because active harm via attention displacement is a stronger claim than no-gain

one_line_idea: Multimodal LLMs are dense-inconsistent across query formats: pointing at a pixel and asking what it is contradicts asking where a named thing is, and cross-format agreement is a label-free quality audit plus a constraint for free improvement.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Cross-format contradictions are frequent and concentrate where the model is wrong in at least one format, so agreement serves as an unsupervised correctness signal, and decoding constrained to cross-format consistency improves both formats without retraining.

one_line_idea: Segmentation-capable multimodal LLMs cannot express spatial uncertainty: their verbalized doubts about mask regions are uncorrelated with actual boundary errors, leaving dense outputs without any usable confidence channel.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Elicited verbal uncertainty about specific mask regions (which side is uncertain, where the boundary might err) will show near-zero correspondence with measured error maps, because no training signal ever connected verbal hedging to spatial error statistics.

one_line_idea: Multi-turn mask correction fails because dialog context does not effectively carry mask state: models treat each correction as a fresh query, and correction success barely exceeds single-turn retry rates.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Current systems lack a functional representation of their previous mask in dialog state, so corrections referencing prior output (the other one, slightly larger) perform no better than independently re-prompting, and explicit mask-state re-injection into context recovers genuine interactive gains.

judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-A-093 (correction oscillation); kept for the dialog-state mechanism in MLLMs

one_line_idea: Visual prompt overlays (marks, boxes, highlights drawn on the image) contaminate the visual stream: they alter dense predictions for unmarked objects, an interference effect that mark-based prompting studies never control.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Overlays cause measurable prediction changes on regions distant from the mark, including segmentation and labeling flips for unmarked objects, with interference growing with overlay salience and proximity, making mark-based results systematically unclean measurements of the intended question.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Visual prompt overlays contaminating predictions for unmarked objects is an interference effect mark-based prompting studies never control.

one_line_idea: High-resolution tiling strategies for multimodal LLMs improve text-reading tasks far more than segmentation because cross-tile attention fails to reintegrate object geometry, producing task-dependent resolution scaling that current unified benchmarks average away.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Tiling benefits capabilities that are tile-local (reading, texture, small-object identity) while leaving tile-spanning capabilities (object extent, boundary continuity, part-whole geometry) largely unimproved, because integration across tile boundaries is mediated only by weak global-view features, and task-decomposed scaling curves will reveal this dissociation.

one_line_idea: Synthetic-data gains in semantic segmentation concentrate on boundary and thin-structure pixels, so pixel-perfect labels rather than scene realism are the active ingredient.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Most of the transfer gain from adding synthetic segmentation data to real training comes from boundary-band and thin-structure pixels where human labels are noisy, not from region interiors where human labels are already reliable.

one_line_idea: Optical flow transfer from synthetic training data is governed by motion statistics rather than photorealism, so matching real motion distributions with crude rendering beats photorealistic data with mismatched motion.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The transfer-relevant factor in synthetic flow data is the distribution of motion magnitudes, discontinuities, and occlusion events, and appearance realism is second-order once basic texture variety exists.

one_line_idea: For object detection, cut-and-paste composition with mediocre blending matches full 3D rendering pipelines once a low realism threshold is passed, making blending quality an over-optimized axis.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Detection transfer depends mainly on object instance diversity and placement plausibility, and blending or rendering realism beyond a crude threshold contributes little, so the two pipelines converge when diversity is equalized.

one_line_idea: The value of synthetic data per task is predicted by the cost of acquiring real labels for that task, not by the size of the domain gap, revealing label scarcity rather than realism as the binding constraint.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Across tasks, the marginal value of synthetic data is a monotone function of real-label acquisition cost and is largely independent of measured appearance gap, because synthetic data competes against the real-label supply curve.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Synthetic-data value predicted by real-label acquisition cost rather than domain gap is an economics-first claim orthogonal to the shard's realism templates.

one_line_idea: Synthetic scene generators systematically under-produce heavy-occlusion configurations, and matching real occlusion statistics yields more detection and segmentation transfer than improving textures.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The occlusion-configuration distribution is a dominant, under-measured axis of the sim-to-real content gap for instance-level tasks, and models trained on occlusion-matched synthetic data transfer better at equal rendering quality.

one_line_idea: For human pose estimation, sampling synthetic poses approximately uniformly over kinematically valid space transfers better than sampling from realistic motion-capture distributions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because pose estimation errors concentrate in the tail of the pose distribution, de-biasing the synthetic pose sampler toward uniform coverage of valid pose space buys more real-world robustness than matching realistic pose frequencies.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Uniform-over-kinematic-space pose sampling beating realistic mocap distributions is an anti-realism sampling claim with a specific counterintuitive direction.

one_line_idea: Synthetic stuff classes transfer nearly for free while thing classes carry most of the sim-to-real gap, motivating hybrid pipelines that render backgrounds and paste real object instances.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The appearance and shape statistics of stuff regions are easy to render acceptably, so the transfer gap concentrates in thing classes, where instance-level texture, wear, and intra-class variety are hard to synthesize.

one_line_idea: A measurable share of the sim-to-real segmentation gap is ontology mismatch between asset-derived synthetic classes and visually defined real classes, fixable by remapping rather than rendering.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Class-mapping errors and definitional mismatches (what counts as road versus parking, building versus wall) contribute a non-trivial, quantifiable fraction of measured sim-to-real error that is misattributed to appearance gap.

one_line_idea: Reconstructing real scenes into neural 3D representations and re-rendering them with perturbed cameras yields dense supervision with real appearance, and this real2sim2real data beats graphics rendering for dense tasks.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Re-rendered reconstructions of real scenes carry near-zero appearance gap while providing multi-view-consistent depth, correspondence, and segmentation propagation labels, and their geometric imperfections harm dense students less than the appearance gap of classical rendering does.

one_line_idea: Domain randomization mostly re-implements strong 2D augmentation, and equally aggressive augmentation of a small real set matches heavy randomization in simulation for many perception tasks.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A large fraction of domain randomization's benefit is expressible as image-space augmentation, so its unique contribution beyond a strong augmentation baseline is limited to 3D-consistent variation (viewpoint, occlusion, geometry) that 2D augmentation cannot mimic.

one_line_idea: Foundation-model backbones have made photorealism largely obsolete for sim-to-real: with frozen pretrained features, low-fidelity rendering transfers as well as high-fidelity rendering.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Pretrained backbones already map low-fidelity and high-fidelity renders of the same content to nearby features, so the marginal transfer value of photorealism collapses once a strong pretrained backbone is used, surviving only for from-scratch training.

one_line_idea: The direction and size of the sim-real transfer asymmetry (sim-to-real versus real-to-sim) is a cheap diagnostic that identifies whether a gap is appearance-driven or content-driven.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Appearance-driven gaps produce roughly symmetric bidirectional degradation, while content-coverage gaps produce asymmetric degradation (the side with narrower content transfers worse outward), so the asymmetry profile classifies gap type without any adaptation experiments.

one_line_idea: Models exploit renderer-specific spectral and noise signatures as shortcuts, and matching low-level image statistics between synthetic and real data removes a large, cheap-to-fix share of the sim-to-real gap.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A significant portion of the sim-to-real appearance gap lives in these camera-pipeline statistics rather than in scene realism, so passing synthetic images through a calibrated camera-pipeline simulation (noise, optics blur, compression) recovers much of the gap at negligible cost.

one_line_idea: Sim-to-real adaptation method rankings established on driving benchmarks do not transfer to other target domains, making the canonical leaderboard a domain artifact.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Adaptation methods encode driving-specific inductive bets (sky-road layout priors, class frequency structure, urban texture statistics), so their relative ranking changes substantially when the same protocol is applied to indoor, agricultural, industrial, or aerial synthetic-real pairs.

one_line_idea: Adapting label-space statistics (class frequencies, object size and count distributions) via resampling beats image-space adaptation for sim-to-real transfer at a fraction of the cost.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A meaningful share of the sim-to-real gap is prior mismatch in label-space statistics, so importance resampling of synthetic data to match target label statistics (estimated from limited target metadata or pseudo-labels) delivers gains competitive with image translation methods.

one_line_idea: For contact-rich robotic perception, physics fidelity dominates visual fidelity in sim-to-real transfer, inverting the effort allocation of typical simulation pipelines.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For tasks whose labels depend on physically plausible object configurations (grasp points, stable poses, cluttered pile perception), errors in physics generate systematically wrong scene content, and this content error transfers worse than rendering error of equal apparent magnitude.

one_line_idea: A large share of the sim-to-real gap lives in normalization statistics, and recalibrating them with a handful of unlabeled real images recovers it without touching any weights.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For sim-trained dense models, recomputing normalization statistics on a small unlabeled real sample captures a disproportionate share of what full unsupervised domain adaptation achieves, implying much of the gap is a first-order input-distribution shift rather than a representational deficiency.

one_line_idea: Generative image translation of synthetic frames corrupts dense labels by hallucinating and deleting content, so translation-based sim-to-real gains are overstated for dense tasks and label-corruption audits should be mandatory.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Translation networks alter content at a non-trivial rate (removing thin structures, hallucinating textures over small objects, shifting boundaries), so the effective training set has systematically corrupted labels, and part of the reported gains would grow if corruption were measured and filtered.

one_line_idea: Weather and lighting randomization in driving simulation covers a thin manifold of real conditions, and a nearest-neighbor coverage audit predicts per-condition transfer failure before any training.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The per-condition transfer performance of sim-trained models is predictable from a coverage measure (distance from each real condition to its nearest synthetic neighbor in a perceptual feature space), making condition-coverage auditing a pre-training diagnostic.

one_line_idea: Pixel-perfect synthetic labels can transfer worse than convention-matched noisy labels because evaluation rewards agreement with human annotator behavior, not with geometric truth.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] When evaluation labels contain systematic human bias, training on exact synthetic labels optimizes a subtly different target, so injecting human-like structured noise into synthetic labels improves benchmark scores even though it degrades geometric truthfulness.

one_line_idea: Foundation-model pseudo-labels carry attribute-correlated structured noise, so noise-robust learning methods validated on uniform synthetic noise fail on the auto-label noise that actually matters now.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Methods that win under injected-flip noise rely on assumptions (noise independent of input given class) violated by model-generated noise, so their ranking collapses or inverts under real auto-label noise.

one_line_idea: Boundary-localized label noise damages segmentation training far more per pixel than interior noise, and a boundary-weighted noise metric predicts downstream harm where raw noise rate fails.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The damage function of dense label noise is strongly spatially non-uniform, concentrated in boundary bands, so two datasets with equal noise rates can differ widely in training value, and a boundary-weighted noise measure recovers the missing predictive power.

one_line_idea: Auto-label noise correlates with example difficulty, so confidence-based label cleaning preferentially deletes hard examples and produces models that score better on clean averages but worse on hard tails.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because label error and example difficulty are confounded in auto-labeled data, cleaning removes a difficulty-biased subset, silently shifting the training distribution toward easy content and degrading tail robustness even as headline metrics improve.

judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-C-070 (QC excludes the hard cases); kept for the training-side cleaning pathology

one_line_idea: The learning-with-noisy-labels leaderboard is a simulation artifact: method rankings under injected noise do not survive on datasets whose noise arose organically from real annotation processes.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Organic annotation noise (guideline ambiguity, attention lapses, systematic misreading of certain classes) has statistical structure absent from injected flips, so a substantial fraction of reported method-over-baseline gains are artifacts of the injection procedure.

one_line_idea: Beyond a threshold noise level, a small verified-clean validation set is worth more per annotation dollar than any quantity of additional noisy training labels, and the exchange rate is measurable.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] In noisy-label regimes there is a quantifiable exchange rate between clean-validation labels and noisy-training labels, and for realistic noise levels the marginal value of the first few hundred clean labels (enabling noise estimation and honest model selection) exceeds that of thousands of additional noisy labels.

one_line_idea: The soft-versus-hard pseudo-label debate reduces to teacher calibration: soft labels win with calibrated teachers and lose with miscalibrated ones, and a calibration measurement predicts the winner per setup.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The value of soft labels is exactly the value of the teacher's uncertainty information, which is positive when calibrated and negative (misleading) when miscalibrated, so teacher calibration error is the moderating variable that reconciles the contradictory literature.

one_line_idea: Most of what is booked as label noise in dense annotation is actually irreducible instruction ambiguity, and synthetic data with a single rendering convention trains models to be confidently wrong about genuinely ambiguous pixels.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A large fraction of dense-label disagreement is ambiguity rather than error, and models trained on convention-deterministic synthetic labels learn artificially low uncertainty on ambiguous regions, harming calibration and downstream decision quality on real data.

one_line_idea: Missing-annotation noise (unlabeled true objects treated as background) dominates wrong-label noise in detection training, and exhaustively labeled synthetic data makes the resulting precision-recall distortion worse, not better.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The dominant label-noise channel in detection is false negatives in real annotation, and mixing exhaustively labeled synthetic data teaches recall behavior that real-benchmark evaluation (scored against incomplete labels) then punishes as false positives, creating a structural precision-recall convention gap.

one_line_idea: The training value of a synthetic sample is predictable at generation time from generator-internal signals, enabling curation before rendering and saving most of the generation compute that post-hoc filtering wastes.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Generator-internal quantities available early in the sampling process (prompt statistics, early-step denoising trajectories, guidance disagreement, latent-space novelty relative to already-generated samples) predict post-hoc curation decisions well enough to skip generating most rejected samples.

one_line_idea: Embedding-coverage diversity metrics saturate long before task utility does, and compositional attribute diversity keeps paying after coverage metrics flatline, exposing a blind spot in curation dashboards.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Beyond a modest scale, additional utility from synthetic data comes from compositional novelty (new attribute-object-relation combinations) that embedding coverage barely registers, so datasets tuned to maximize coverage metrics underperform datasets tuned for compositional spread at equal size.

one_line_idea: For low-resource target domains, curating real web data to match a synthetic reference distribution beats curating synthetic data to match limited real samples, reversing the standard curation direction.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A well-designed synthetic distribution can encode domain knowledge (coverage of conditions, balanced compositions) more faithfully than a small real sample encodes the true distribution, so using synthetic data as the reference to retrieve and filter abundant unlabeled web data yields better training sets than the reverse direction.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Curating real web data to match a synthetic reference reverses the standard curation direction; nobody else inverts the arrow.

one_line_idea: Difficulty-based hard-example mining on synthetic pools preferentially selects generator failure artifacts rather than genuinely hard content, actively injecting shortcut features into training.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Loss-based mining cannot distinguish these two sources, and because artifacts are systematically weird, mining concentrates them, teaching students artifact-specific features and degrading real-data transfer relative to random selection at high mining rates.

one_line_idea: Data-pruning conclusions invert with scale on synthetic pools: pruning helps at small training budgets and hurts at large ones, with a predictable crossover that current papers ignore by evaluating at single scales.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] On synthetic pools, aggressive pruning improves results in data-rich-relative-to-capacity regimes but harms in capacity-rich regimes where models can exploit long-tail redundancy, producing a systematic scale-dependent sign flip with an estimable crossover point.

one_line_idea: Source-level scheduling (synthetic-then-real annealing) dominates example-level curriculum within synthetic data, so curation effort spent ordering synthetic examples is largely wasted.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The performance-relevant scheduling decision is when to transition between synthetic and real sources, while within-synthetic example ordering contributes negligibly once the source schedule is right, because the domain shift dwarfs within-domain difficulty structure.

one_line_idea: Influence-style valuation against a real validation set reveals that most of a typical synthetic pool has near-zero or negative training value, with the positive value concentrated in a small identifiable slice.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The distribution of per-example value in synthetic pools is heavy-tailed and partly negative: a minority of examples drive the real-data gains, a majority are inert, and an identifiable subset actively hurts, so value-targeted selection can match full-pool training with a fraction of the data.

one_line_idea: Generative synthetic-data utility scales with distinct-prompt count, not image count: images-per-prompt beyond a small number is nearly wasted compute, making prompt engineering the real dataset-size lever.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Within-prompt samples are so correlated that their marginal utility decays after a handful, so at fixed generation compute, spending on prompt diversity strictly dominates spending on samples-per-prompt, and the effective dataset size is closer to the prompt count than the image count.

one_line_idea: Procedural and abstract-image pretraining works by installing generic early-layer filters, so its benefit saturates at small scale and vanishes for foundation-scale models with long real-data training.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The benefit is confined to installing low-level filter structure that small models learn slowly from limited real data, so it shrinks as model scale, real-data volume, or training length grows, approaching zero in the foundation regime.

one_line_idea: Training students on generator-produced data is distillation, not discovery: it accelerates learning toward the generator's knowledge but cannot exceed it, and the ceiling is measurable.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For distribution-level knowledge, generator-produced data acts as a compressed re-serialization of the generator's training distribution: students converge faster but asymptote at or below the generator-implied ceiling, with genuine exceedance possible only where an external signal (filtering by verifiable criteria, real labels) injects information the generator lacked.

one_line_idea: Synthetic data helps foundation models where real data is thin: a density-targeted synthesis policy that generates in low-density regions of the real distribution beats uniform synthesis at equal budget.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The marginal value of a synthetic sample is inversely related to real-data density at its location, so estimating the real corpus density and generating preferentially in sparse regions yields larger pretraining improvements than uniform or popularity-weighted generation.

one_line_idea: Synthetic captions improve benchmark retrieval scores while quietly degrading robustness under distribution shift because they homogenize the text distribution that contrastive training consumes.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Generated captions occupy a narrower stylistic and semantic register than organic alt-text, and this text-side homogenization reduces the diversity pressure that gives contrastive models their distribution-shift robustness, creating a benchmark-robustness tradeoff invisible in standard reporting.

one_line_idea: Rendering-based synthetic pretraining transfers to geometry-loaded tasks and not to semantics-loaded ones, and a task's geometry-semantics loading predicts its synthetic-pretraining benefit.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Synthetic rendering pretraining installs geometric competence (depth, correspondence, contours) that transfers broadly, while its semantic content is too narrow to transfer, so the benefit across downstream tasks is predictable from a geometry-versus-semantics task decomposition.

one_line_idea: Self-supervised objectives differ systematically in synthetic-data tolerance: reconstruction-style objectives degrade less on synthetic pretraining data than contrastive ones, so data provenance should drive objective choice.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Contrastive objectives lean on fine-grained instance diversity that synthetic corpora lack (duplicates, mode concentration), while reconstruction objectives extract local statistics that synthetic data preserves, so the objective ranking flips between real and synthetic corpora.

one_line_idea: Tagging synthetic samples with a provenance token during pretraining recovers most of the performance lost to synthetic contamination, versus silently mixing, at essentially zero cost.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Conditioning on a provenance signal during training lets the model separate synthetic-specific statistics from real ones (analogous to domain conditioning), so tagged mixing preserves real-data performance that silent mixing loses, and the tag can be dropped or set to real at inference.

one_line_idea: Students inherit generator fingerprints from synthetic training data strongly enough that the generator identity is recoverable from student behavior, enabling training-data supply-chain forensics.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Generator-specific artifacts shape student features and error patterns in identifiable ways, so a classifier over student behavior (predictions on probe images, feature statistics) can attribute which generator produced a substantial part of the student's training data.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Generator-fingerprint recovery from student behavior enables training-data supply-chain forensics; an application claim unique in the pool.

one_line_idea: Generating training data with a large generator to train a small task model beats direct real-data training only inside a predictable regime boundary defined by the task's distance from the generator's training distribution.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The pattern works when the task distribution is well inside the generator's training support (generation acts as retrieval-plus-relabeling) and fails as the task moves off-support, so an off-support distance measure predicts the sign of the synthetic-versus-real advantage.

one_line_idea: Self-training loops plateau because of diversity collapse in what gets auto-labeled, not noise accumulation, and an entropy audit of accepted pseudo-labels predicts the plateau before it arrives.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The binding constraint is that confidence-thresholded acceptance concentrates on an ever-narrower slice of the data distribution each round, so the marginal information per round collapses even when accepted-label accuracy stays high, making diversity collapse rather than noise the plateau mechanism.

one_line_idea: Text-to-image augmentation gains are bounded by the generator's within-class diversity, which is far below real data, and a generator-side recall measurement predicts the augmentation ceiling per class.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For each class, augmentation value is capped by how much of the real within-class variation the generator can actually produce (its class-conditional recall), so measuring generator recall per class predicts which classes benefit and where the gains saturate.

one_line_idea: Editing real images beats generating from scratch for augmentation at equal budget because edits preserve real image statistics while still adding controlled variation, especially for dense tasks.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Full generation pays a distribution-shift tax on every pixel, while editing pays it only on modified regions, so at matched variation injected, edit-based augmentation transfers better, with the advantage largest for dense tasks where unmodified regions retain exact real labels.

one_line_idea: The best use of generative models for dense tasks is generating labels for real images rather than images for synthetic labels, inverting the standard generation pipeline.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For a fixed generative model and budget, extracting dense pseudo-labels (masks, depth, correspondences) for abundant real images yields better student training data than generating synthetic images with perfect labels, because appearance fidelity matters more than label fidelity at current quality levels.

one_line_idea: Published diffusion-augmentation gains shrink dramatically against modern strong-augmentation baselines, surviving mainly in low-data regimes, and a reproduction matrix would recalibrate the field's expectations.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A substantial portion of reported generative-augmentation gains duplicates what strong conventional augmentation already provides, so under equalized modern baselines the marginal gain concentrates in genuinely low-data regimes and vanishes at scale.

judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-C-063/C-064 (scale-dependent nulls, generator-style-dependent gains); kept for the reproduction-matrix design

one_line_idea: Web-crawl vintages carry rising synthetic fractions, and models pretrained on different crawl vintages show behavior drift attributable to synthetic contamination, making vintage a measurable data-quality variable.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Synthetic fraction is a systematic function of crawl date, and models pretrained on later vintages exhibit measurable behavioral shifts (texture statistics preferences, structural-detail handling, robustness profile changes) that track the contamination level rather than content drift alone.

one_line_idea: Bilevel-optimal data generation (generate to directly maximize student validation improvement) is approximable by first-order gradient matching at a tiny fraction of the cost, capturing most of its gain.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The bilevel objective's value is dominated by its first-order component (generating samples whose training gradients align with the student's validation-loss gradient), so a cheap gradient-matching guidance signal on the generator captures most of the bilevel gain without inner-loop retraining.

one_line_idea: Deliberately generating realistic near-miss hard negatives improves fine-grained discrimination more than generating additional positives, making negative synthesis the underused half of generative augmentation.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Generators can be steered to produce calibrated near-miss negatives (almost-correct examples crossing a decision boundary), and at matched budgets such negatives sharpen decision boundaries more than additional positives, especially for fine-grained and safety-relevant distinctions.

one_line_idea: Generated video is a poor training source for temporal representations because its artifacts are temporal, and hybrid data (generated appearance with real motion) beats end-to-end video generation for training video models.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because the artifact budget of video generation concentrates in temporal structure, students trained on generated video learn degenerate temporal features, and composing real motion sources (real videos, motion capture, flow fields) with generated appearance yields strictly better temporal representation learning at matched budgets.

one_line_idea: Transfer from graphics data scales with distinct 3D asset count without saturating, while realism knobs saturate early, so generation budgets should buy assets, not rendering quality.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Downstream transfer follows a slowly decaying power law in unique asset count (each new asset adds instance-level variety models still need) but saturates quickly in rendering-quality improvements, so the asset axis dominates at every realistic budget.

one_line_idea: Tasks defined only through synthetic supervision, like intrinsic decomposition, may have models that learned renderer conventions rather than physics, and a real-light-transport audit would expose the gap.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models for such tasks fit the specific approximations of the generating renderer (its shading model, light-transport shortcuts) rather than physical structure, so they degrade systematically on real scenes with measured ground truth and on synthetic scenes from physically different renderers.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Synthetic-only-supervised tasks (intrinsic decomposition) possibly learning renderer conventions rather than physics attacks a task's epistemic foundation, not its methods.

one_line_idea: Layout realism (object co-occurrence and physical support relations) transfers more than appearance realism, so scene-grammar investment beats shading investment at equal cost.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models consume contextual priors from training scenes, so violating layout statistics injects wrong priors that hurt transfer more than flat shading does, making scene-grammar quality the higher-return realism axis.

one_line_idea: Procedural generation parameters can be optimized directly against downstream validation performance with black-box methods, because the loss over generation parameters is smoother than assumed.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Downstream validation performance varies smoothly over generation parameters, so sample-efficient black-box optimization with cheap proxy trainings (small models, short schedules) can find substantially better parameter settings than expert defaults within a modest number of cycles.

one_line_idea: Camera and ISP simulation parameters matter more for geometric-task transfer than scene content, and calibrating the virtual camera to the target device closes more depth-estimation gap than content matching.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For depth, pose, and structure tasks, the mismatch between idealized virtual cameras and real device pipelines is a first-order transfer factor, so calibrating simulation to the target camera (intrinsics, distortion, ISP) yields larger gains than equivalent effort on content realism.

one_line_idea: Rendered-human training data shows an uncanny-valley non-monotonicity: mid-realism renders transfer worse than either stylized or high-realism renders for person-centric tasks.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Transfer to real person-centric tasks is non-monotone in realism: stylized data teaches transferable structure without competing appearance cues, high-realism data matches real appearance, but mid-realism data creates features aligned with neither distribution, producing a measurable performance dip.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Uncanny-valley non-monotonicity for rendered humans (mid-realism worst) is a non-monotone transfer claim; every template in the family assumes monotone axes.

one_line_idea: Generator quality metrics like distribution-distance scores are nearly uncorrelated with the training utility of generated data, and the field needs utility-specific metrics rather than borrowed perceptual ones.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Across generators, sampling configurations, and curation choices, perceptual distribution metrics rank synthetic datasets in an order weakly related to their measured training utility, because utility depends on coverage, label alignment, and redundancy that perceptual metrics compress or ignore.

judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-C-037 (gameable generative metrics); kept for the utility-correlation (not gameability) claim

one_line_idea: Train-on-synthetic-test-on-real rankings of synthetic datasets flip across student architectures, so dataset-superiority claims made with one architecture are architecture-conditional statements in disguise.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Synthetic datasets differ in which model inductive biases their artifacts and distribution choices interact with, so dataset rankings measured with different student families (convolutional, attention-based, different capacities) disagree materially.

one_line_idea: A cheap probe suite over frozen foundation features can predict the full-training utility of a synthetic dataset, replacing most train-to-evaluate cycles in curation loops.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The information that determines full-training utility (coverage of the target distribution, label alignment, redundancy, artifact load) is measurable with lightweight probes over frozen pretrained features, yielding a predictor that ranks candidate datasets nearly as well as full training does.

one_line_idea: Synthetic test sets systematically compress model rankings because generators regress toward typical instances, making synthetic evaluation optimistically biased and rank-unstable for model comparison.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Generators produce instances closer to distribution modes than real sampling does at matched nominal difficulty, so synthetic test sets under-represent the tail cases that differentiate strong models, compressing measured gaps and destabilizing rankings relative to real tests.

one_line_idea: Synthetic data quality is two independent axes, fidelity and coverage, that trade off differently per task, and single-scalar quality reporting systematically misleads adoption decisions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Downstream tasks weight fidelity and coverage differently (dense recognition favoring coverage, fine-grained discrimination favoring fidelity), so scalar rankings routinely recommend the wrong dataset for a given task, and two-axis reporting would flip a measurable fraction of adoption decisions.

one_line_idea: Generators have seen the benchmarks: synthetic training data leaks evaluation content through generator memorization, inflating synthetic-data results in ways standard contamination checks never audit.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Prompting generators in the semantic vicinity of benchmark content produces training images that leak test-set-specific information (near-duplicate compositions, distinctive instances), measurably inflating benchmark scores of models trained on such synthetic data.

judge_c.wave1_adjacent: W13-P1-C-023 (contamination); kept for the generator-memorization leakage pathway

one_line_idea: Reported synthetic-data gains are confounded by asymmetric tuning effort, and equal-tuning-budget re-evaluation would deflate a measurable share of published improvements.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Under matched hyperparameter search budgets for both arms, a substantial fraction of published synthetic-data improvements shrinks or disappears, and the surviving gains identify the subset of techniques with real effect.

one_line_idea: Per-image accounting hides the cost of synthetic data: under per-FLOP accounting that includes generation compute, many synthetic-data results are net-negative versus simply training longer on real data.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] When total compute (generation plus training) is the equalized resource, the synthetic-data advantage shrinks systematically, and for a meaningful class of settings the same compute spent on longer real-data training or stronger augmentation wins outright.

one_line_idea: Batch-generated synthetic data violates the i.i.d. assumption through shared seeds, prompts, and scheduler state, and decorrelating generation batches yields free training gains.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Within-batch correlation in generated data reduces the effective sample size and injects correlated gradient noise, so generation protocols that enforce cross-batch decorrelation (seed spacing, prompt interleaving, setting jitter) improve downstream training at identical image counts.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Batch-generation i.i.d. violation via shared seeds/prompts/scheduler state is an overlooked statistical mechanism with a free mitigation.

one_line_idea: More realism is not monotonically better: past a threshold, realistic synthesis re-imports the real world's spurious correlations that cruder randomized data had removed, hurting robustness.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Part of synthetic data's value is inadvertent bias removal, so as synthesis approaches full realism it restores the real distribution's shortcuts, producing a non-monotone robustness curve where intermediate randomization outperforms maximal realism on out-of-distribution evaluation.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Realism re-importing the real world's spurious correlations past a threshold is the anti-thesis of the realism-helps default and of naive domain randomization. Protected tension.

one_line_idea: Synthetic data optimized to match today's distribution is optimized for the wrong target when deployment shifts the distribution, and shift-anticipating synthesis beats distribution-matching synthesis.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For deployments with predictable shift structure (seasonal cycles, hardware upgrades, behavior adaptation), synthesizing data for plausible future distributions rather than the present one yields better performance over the deployment window, and the advantage is largest where retraining cadence is slow.

one_line_idea: Synthetic data is assumed privacy-safe by construction, but generator memorization leaks training individuals, and the utility cost of verified non-memorization is unknown and possibly severe.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For visual data containing people and identifiable scenes, the achievable frontier between measured re-identification risk and downstream utility is materially worse than assumed, and enforcing verified non-memorization (filtering or training constraints) costs a quantifiable, possibly large, share of the synthetic data's utility.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Privacy leakage through generator memorization in 'privacy-safe by construction' synthetic data, and the unknown utility cost of verified non-memorization.

one_line_idea: The domain gap is treated as a scalar when it is a decomposable vector over appearance, content, sensor, and label-convention factors, and interventions are systematically misattributed as a result.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A factor-wise decomposition protocol (controlled swaps of appearance, content statistics, sensor pipeline, and label convention between synthetic and real) yields stable, additive-enough gap components, and re-analyzing standard interventions against components reveals widespread misattribution of their effects.

one_line_idea: The student-cannot-exceed-teacher assumption fails for dense geometry: averaging noisy generator-derived labels across many views or samples lets students surpass their labeling teacher measurably.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] When teacher errors are partly independent across views, augmentations, or samples of the same underlying geometry, aggregate supervision (multi-view consistency fusing many noisy teacher estimates) carries more information than any single teacher output, letting students exceed teacher accuracy in a predictable regime defined by error correlation.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Students exceeding the labeling teacher for dense geometry via multi-view/sample averaging is the anti-thesis of F-052's ceiling. Protected tension.

one_line_idea: Real and synthetic data follow different scaling exponents that interact, and a two-term joint scaling law fitted from pilot runs predicts the optimal real-synthetic mix at any budget.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Real-data volume, synthetic-data volume, and their interaction determine loss through a stable parametric surface (task-dependent exponents plus a substitution term), fittable from small pilot grids and extrapolable to larger budgets with useful accuracy.

one_line_idea: Small domain-specialized generators beat giant general generators as training-data engines at equal generation compute, contradicting the bigger-generator-is-better default.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For a fixed generation-compute budget, a small domain-tuned generator produces more useful training data (more samples, better domain coverage, fewer irrelevant modes) than a large general model, except when the task requires compositional breadth only the large model has.

one_line_idea: Synthetic datasets depreciate faster than real datasets as deployment distributions and conventions drift, and measuring dataset half-life reveals different amortization economics for the two data types.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Training value decays with dataset age for both data types, but synthetic datasets decay faster because they inherit era-specific generator artifacts, prompt fashions, and convention choices on top of world drift, giving them a measurably shorter half-life and worse amortized economics than per-image costs suggest.

judge_c.anomaly_note: Dataset half-life / depreciation-rate asymmetry between synthetic and real data introduces an amortization-economics variable nobody measures.
